title: Leonida & Vice City
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI returns to the fictional state of Leonida, a sun-bleached peninsula of causeways, wetlands, and neon coastline. Vice City is its loudest address: a modern resort metropolis built for money, music, and bad decisions. The revealed story follows Jason and Lucia through a state that treats every sunset like a premiere.

title: Vice City, 1986
summary: The 2002 classic turned the series into a period piece: pastel suits, synth-pop, oceanfront clubs, and a criminal economy with a taste for chrome. Tommy Vercetti arrives in a city that rewards confidence and punishes sentiment, and the game's radio dial becomes as memorable as its skyline.

title: San Andreas, 1992
summary: Three cities, one enormous state, and a homecoming story about family, loyalty, and territory. San Andreas mixes early-90s West Coast culture with a road-trip structure: Los Santos, San Fierro, and Las Venturas each bring a different rhythm, skyline, and kind of trouble.

title: Los Santos, 2013
summary: Grand Theft Auto V splits its story across three protagonists and one sprawling satirical metropolis. Michael, Franklin, and Trevor move between heists, hobbies, and the entertainment industry's endless appetite for reinvention. The result is a West Coast playground built around planning, improvisation, and spectacle.

title: Liberty City, 2008
summary: Grand Theft Auto IV trades sunshine for overcast steel. Niko Bellic arrives in Liberty City chasing an idea of success and finds a colder city of immigrants, debts, and old wars. The game's tone is grounded, its streets dense, and its story less about empire than about the cost of trying to leave one behind.

title: The Warriors, 1979
summary: Rockstar's brawler expands Walter Hill's cult film into a long, dangerous night across a stylized New York. Gangs own the subway map, turf is measured in blocks and platforms, and the journey home becomes the whole story. The game's look leans on graffiti, turnstiles, and fluorescent light.

title: The Frontier, 1899
summary: Red Dead Redemption 2 is a prequel about the end of an era: a gang trying to stay useful while the world builds fences and railroads around it. Snow, swamp, prairie, and city all share the same slow rhythm. The frontier here is less a place to conquer than a story people keep telling themselves.

title: Bullworth Academy, 2006
summary: Bully trades city blocks for school corridors, cliques, and small-town gossip. Jimmy Hopkins navigates a private academy where the hierarchy is absurdly serious and the calendar is a social weapon. It is a Rockstar game about territory at a much smaller scale, with the same eye for satire.

title: The franchise, from 1997
summary: Grand Theft Auto began as a top-down crime game from DMA Design and grew into one of the most recognizable open-world series in the medium. Each era added a new city, a new voice, and a new way to measure freedom: from arcade chaos to cinematic scale.

title: Rockstar Games
summary: Rockstar Games was established as a publishing label under Take-Two Interactive in 1998. Its studios have built a catalog across crime, westerns, noir, and schoolyard satire, with a house style that favors dense worlds, strong radio soundtracks, and sharply observed fiction.

title: Tommy Vercetti
summary: A made man with a long memory and a short temper. Tommy arrives in Vice City expecting a debt to be settled and decides to collect the whole city instead. His story is about refusing to be anyone's subordinate.

title: Carl 'CJ' Johnson
summary: A returning son who spends most of San Andreas trying to keep his family together while the city pulls it apart. CJ is loyal, practical, and increasingly aware that loyalty is not a plan.

title: Niko Bellic
summary: A war veteran chasing a ghost through Liberty City. Niko's story is about the difference between the life he was promised and the one he keeps choosing.

title: Michael, Franklin & Trevor
summary: Three protagonists with incompatible ideas about success. Michael wants meaning, Franklin wants distance from the block, and Trevor wants to be the only honest person in the room.

title: Jason & Lucia
summary: The revealed leads of GTA VI: a partnership built on trust in a state that rewards self-interest. Their story is framed as a modern crime romance rather than a lone-wolf rise.

title: Grove Street Families
summary: A neighbourhood outfit defined by history, loyalty, and a losing war for territory. Grove Street is less a gang than a memory of one, which is exactly what makes it worth fighting for.

title: The Lost MC
summary: A motorcycle club held together by tradition and torn apart by ego. The Lost are at their most dangerous when they are trying to prove they still matter.

title: The Vercetti Organisation
summary: A crew built out of borrowed loyalty and purchased property. By the end of 1986 it controls clubs, businesses, and the kind of silence that money can buy.

title: The gangs of 1979
summary: The Warriors turns the New York night into a patchwork of turf, colours, and grudges. Every bridge is a border and every train car is somebody's territory.

title: Bullworth's cliques
summary: Bullworth Academy is a small world with big politics: jocks, preppies, greasers, nerds, and everyone else trying to survive the timetable. The satire is sharp because the stakes feel real.

title: Liberty City, 1997
summary: The original Liberty City was a top-down grid of three islands, built for short, chaotic crime sprees rather than a cinematic story. Its paper-thin premise — rise through the criminal ranks by any means — set the template the series would spend decades refining.

title: London, 1969
summary: The London expansion traded Liberty City for a period British capital of tight streets, mod culture, and very different cars. It was an early sign that the series could reskin its formula around a specific place and era instead of just another American city.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Grand Theft Auto: London 1969"

title: Ricardo Diaz
summary: A wealthy Vice City drug baron whose mansion, connections, and paranoia make him both a useful patron and an obvious target. Diaz represents the older criminal order that Tommy Vercetti learns to read, then replace.

title: Lance Vance
summary: A charming, resentful partner whose family history ties him to Vice City's drug trade. Lance works best as a mirror for Tommy: both want a way in, but only one is willing to wait for it.

title: The Malibu Club
summary: A neon nightclub on Vice City's waterfront that doubles as a front for planning bigger jobs. Buying the Malibu is one of the story's clearest status shifts: from hired muscle to someone with a venue, a crew, and a reason to be feared.

title: Big Smoke
summary: A larger-than-life Grove Street figure whose appetites and ambitions slowly pull him away from the neighbourhood. His arc is one of the series' sharpest arguments that loyalty and self-interest can wear the same face for years.

title: Ryder
summary: A restless Grove Street member with a short fuse and a long memory. Ryder's streetwise bravado hides how quickly the ground under the set is shifting, making him one of San Andreas' most complicated early allies.

title: Frank Tenpenny
summary: A corrupt Los Santos police officer who treats the law as a private enforcement tool. Tenpenny is the system-level villain of San Andreas: not a rival gang, but the person supposedly keeping the city in order.

title: The Ballas
summary: A rival Los Santos set defined by colour, territory, and a long-running feud with Grove Street. The Ballas are less a single organisation than a pressure system that shapes every block in the city.

title: Roman Bellic
summary: Niko's cousin and the source of Liberty City's warmest and most unreliable promises. Roman sells optimism as a survival strategy, which makes his setbacks feel less like plot twists and more like the city doing what it does.

title: The Pegorino Family
summary: An old-guard Liberty City crime family trying to stay relevant while newer crews rewrite the rules. Their declining influence is a useful window into GTA IV's central idea: the city rewards the next arrangement, not the last one.

title: Lamar Davis
summary: Franklin's friend, business partner, and occasional liability, with a comic rhythm that masks real ambition. Lamar keeps the Los Santos story grounded in the block even when the protagonists are flying between heists.

title: Blaine County
summary: The desert-and-farmland half of GTA V's map, where small towns, meth labs, and long empty roads sit beside a national park. It is the series' most deliberate contrast to a city: the same freedom, with fewer people to perform for.

title: The Leonida Keys
summary: A chain of islands and causeways at the southern edge of Leonida, shown in GTA VI's map material as a slower, stranger counterpoint to Vice City. Long water roads and small communities make it the kind of place where local knowledge matters more than horsepower.

title: Grassrivers
summary: Leonida's wetland interior, built around airboats, alligators, and roads that disappear into water. The area gives GTA VI a rural counterweight to the neon coast and a reminder that the state is bigger than its skyline.

title: Arthur Morgan
summary: A career outlaw and the emotional centre of Red Dead Redemption 2, caught between loyalty to his gang and the evidence that the world is closing around it. Arthur's story is less about redemption as a prize than about choosing what kind of person to be before the end.

title: Dutch van der Linde
summary: The charismatic leader whose vision of freedom keeps a gang together long after the plan has stopped working. Dutch is the frontier's answer to a GTA kingpin: a man whose confidence is both the reason people follow and the reason they cannot leave.
attribution: Adapted from GTA Wiki, "Dutch van der Linde"

title: Saint Denis
summary: Red Dead's New Orleans analogue: a humid, industrial city of streetcars, press, and old money. It is the point where the frontier stops feeling like an escape and starts looking like a system with paperwork.

title: Jimmy Hopkins
summary: A teenager dropped into Bullworth Academy and forced to learn its hierarchy faster than he can make friends. Jimmy is a Rockstar protagonist in miniature: stubborn, resourceful, and happier solving a problem with a plan than with an apology.

title: Gary Smith
summary: Bullworth's most manipulative student, who treats every clique as a lever and every friendship as a temporary tool. Gary turns the school's social map into a strategy game, then dares everyone else to keep up.

title: Swan
summary: The Warriors' acting leader on the long ride home, carrying the weight of a crew that has just been framed. Swan's quiet authority is the centre of the story: less a loud hero than the person everyone checks for before making a move.

title: Luther
summary: The Rogues leader whose shot at the rally turns a citywide gathering into a nightlong manhunt. Luther is a small-time operator with a talent for making other people pay for his ambition.
